title: Research Associate - Marine Behavioural Ecology Group (Fixed-term)
description:
Research Associate - Marine Behavioural Ecology Group (Fixed-term)
We are seeking a highly motivated computational researcher for a six-month project in the Marine Behavioural Ecology Group (MBEG), in the Department of Zoology at the University of Cambridge. The project will investigate how individual movement, predator-prey interactions and social interactions shape fish behaviour, using trajectory data and simulation-based approaches.
Fish trajectories provide a detailed record of how individuals move and interact, but extracting the behavioural rules underlying those patterns requires careful data processing and quantitative analysis. You will develop and apply reproducible workflows for trajectory reconstruction, quality control, temporal alignment and the extraction of kinematic and spatial measures. You will use these data to analyse individual and group movement, predator-prey interactions, and develop agent-based and evolutionary simulations to test how behavioural rules and selection processes could generate the patterns observed.
This is an opportunity to work at the interface of computational modelling and behavioural ecology. You will exercise technical judgement in selecting and developing analytical methods, and contribute to interpreting and presenting results through research outputs and reports. The work will involve close collaboration with the Principal Investigator and other members of MBEG, while requiring independence in managing and progressing your computational research.
The postholder will join a collaborative research group studying animal movement, collective behaviour and predator-prey interactions. They may also contribute to research discussions and seminars, and support student research or skills development where appropriate.
For more information, please refer to the Further Particulars document.

description:

A clinical research associate position is available working on a collaborative project to develop diagnostic and prognostic tools for coronary artery disease, as part of a multi-disciplinary team led by Professor Martin Bennett at the Department of Medicine, University of Cambridge, where the position will be based.
Cardiovascular disease is the largest cause of death worldwide, and new diagnostics and treatments are needed, particularly in those at highest risk. In collaboration with the Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics, Centre for Mathematics Sciences, Cambridge, we have developed an AI-based machine learning algorithm to analyse intracoronary images and identify high-risk patients and assess the efficacy of drugs to prevent or treat disease. The clinical research associate will work within a growing team of clinical and non-clinical scientists to further develop this and other tools for clinical use, focusing on image co-registration, segmentation, and post-processing to generate outputs suitable for clinical decision making. We are particularly looking for candidates with experience in invasive coronary image processing for real-world problems, and experience with relevant image analysis software would be very advantageous.
Further information on the project from Professor Martin Bennett (mrb24@ cam.ac.uk).

title: Research Associate - Molecular Virology and Viral Emergence (Fixed Term)
description:
We are seeking an enthusiastic and motivated researcher to join the laboratory of Dr Suzannah Rihn at the Cambridge Institute of Therapeutic Immunology and Infectious Disease (CITIID), University of Cambridge.
Emerging and re-emerging viruses pose a continuing threat to human health. Understanding the molecular mechanisms that enable viruses to cross species barriers, adapt to new hosts and establish infections in humans is essential for improving our preparedness for future epidemics and pandemics. Our research uses a combination of molecular virology, cell biology and experimental models of virus infection to investigate the interactions between viruses and their hosts that determine the potential for viral emergence.
The successful candidate will contribute to an exciting research programme investigating the molecular determinants of viral cross-species transmission. Working as part of a collaborative research team, they will use a range of experimental approaches to investigate how viral and host factors influence infection, replication and adaptation. The project will provide opportunities to develop expertise in molecular virology, including cell culture, molecular cloning, viral reverse genetics and functional assays of virus infection.
The postholder will be expected to plan and conduct experiments, analyse and interpret data, maintain accurate research records and contribute to the preparation of scientific manuscripts and presentations. They will also participate in laboratory meetings, contribute to the wider scientific activities of the group and collaborate with colleagues within CITIID and beyond.
Applicants should have, or be close to obtaining, a PhD in biological, biochemical or biomedical sciences, with relevant experience in molecular biology or virology. We are particularly interested in candidates with experience studying virus infection, a strong background in experimental molecular virology and an emerging track record of scientific publicatio

title: Research Assistant / Research Associate (Fixed Term)
description:
Prof Maura Malpetti is looking for an enthusiastic Research Assistant/Associate to join her lab at the Cambridge University Department of Clinical Neurosciences. The post is part of a Cambridge-based program aiming to investigate inflammation in frontotemporal dementia and accelerate the development of treatments for dementia. To this end, we established a multi-centre study, the UK-wide Open Network for Frontotemporal dementia Innovation Research (ON-FIRE), which involves data collection from >40 sites across the UK.

The role will involve computational analyses of blood-derived data - not wet-lab analyses on the samples - and leading academic and industry collaborations.
The postholder will develop pipelines to combine multimodal data, linking blood samples to NHS digital records, clinical longitudinal data, genetics and neuroimages (MRI and PET). You will lead computational analyses on biomarkers data, polygenic risk score calculations, and immunophenotyping data. You will drive the project, develop and deliver the study's research objectives and be well equipped to present developments and key findings to relevant stakeholders.
For this post, you will have an undergraduate and/or a PhD in Bioinformatics, Statistics, Neurosciences or related discipline. You will have in-depth of knowledge of biostatistics, and related research methods and applications. Experience with machine learning algorithms and strong programming skills using platforms such as MATLAB, R, Bash and Python will be essential.

description:
The UK Hub for Predictive and AI-Enabled Human Disease Models is a UK national research initiative funded by the Medical Research Council (MRC), which aims to translate academic New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) into validated, industry-ready systems. They will develop and optimise organoid culture systems, support the introduction of automated culture workflows and undertake molecular and epigenetic profiling, including DNA methylation profiling, spatial transcriptomics and other multi-omics approaches.
The role will involve independent and collaborative research, including the development of functional assays and application of molecular and cellular techniques to characterise intestinal organoid models. The postholder will work closely with researchers, clinicians and external partners to support the development of robust, reproducible and predictive human disease models.

Physics-Guided Representation Learning from Free Energy Perturbation Data for Affinity Prediction and Candidate Down-Selection
, aims to develop novel machine-learning methods for predicting molecular binding affinities and supporting decision-making in drug discovery.
Free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations provide valuable information about how strongly candidate drug molecules bind to their biological targets, but these calculations are computationally expensive. This project will investigate how machine-learning models can extract richer information from FEP data and experimental measurements, combining physical principles with modern representation-learning techniques.
The research will involve developing and evaluating new statistical and machine-learning methods, with access to both public benchmark datasets and AstraZeneca's industrial drug-discovery expertise and data.

title: Psychology of Unethical Decisions and Public Trust (Fixed Term)
description:
The Cambridge ESRC Doctoral Training Partnership [CAM-DTP] is pleased to offer an knowledge exchange studentship available for admission in October 2027.
The studentship will be co-supervised by Dr Jon Roozenbeek (Department of Psychology), Dr Lee de Wit (Department of Psychology) and Moira Nicolson (UK Cabinet Office)
Project description: 
Unethical decision-making is as a major societal problem. For instance, the Grenfell and Hillsborough disasters in the UK were preceded by a chain of decision failures. title: Postdoctoral Research Associate (Fixed Term)
description:
Postdoctoral Research Associate
Molecular and Cellular Biology of Mitochondrial Disease Models
The University of Cambridge wishes to appoint a talented postdoctoral research associate to join the research group of Prof Rita Horvath at the Department of Clinical Neurosciences and the John Van Geest Brain Repair Centre.
The position is part of a research grant from the joint call of the Action Medical Research and Action for AT, to characterise novel biomarkers of ataxia telangiectasia that support monitoring neurological progression and measuring treatment effect. The focus of your work will be to study how neuron-specific biomarkers reflect the progression of ataxia and how these change on treatment with novel antisense oligonucleotides.
You will use cutting-edge technologies, including functional studies on neuronal stem cells and human neurons. Proteomics, RNA sequencing and other omics technologies will be performed to identify the molecular mechanism of neurodegeneration and ataxia in children and adults. The over-arching aim of the research group is to develop new treatments for mitochondrial diseases and other inherited rare neuromuscular diseases using a combination of genomic, cell biology and specialized assays. You will have access to a team of experienced bioinformaticians, but have the opportunity to be trained and perform independent in-depth bioinformatic analysis of large datasets. You will have access to clinical samples from the MitoCamb neurogenetics clinic, to apply and translate novel technology and insights towards a human disease context.
We anticipate this work will lead to high-profile publications based on our track-record: Nat Comm 2026 PMID:42324264; Nat Comm 2023 PMID:36823193; Brain 2026 PMID:42634970.
The role will be located within the John Van Geest Centre for Brain Repair on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus, with state-of-the-art facilities available to group members.

description:

Applications are invited for a Senior Research Associate to work with Professor Steven F. Lee in the Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry, University of Cambridge.
The post forms part of a translational research programme developing an imaging based drug discovery platform for neurodegenerative disease. Using quantitative single molecule imaging, the programme will characterise small protein assemblies and determine how candidate compounds alter their formation, structure and abundance. The initial focus is alpha synuclein aggregation in Parkinson's disease.
The programme will develop, miniaturise and validate a higher throughput assay, undertake compound screening and generate quantitative datasets linking compound treatment to changes in protein assembly. Working with Cambridge researchers and external academic and translational partners, the successful applicant will help develop the technology into a robust, externally deployable drug discovery platform.
The successful applicant will take substantial independent responsibility for:
Developing and validating quantitative single molecule imaging assays for protein aggregation.
Establishing reproducible workflows for higher throughput compound screening.
Performing screening experiments and developing quantitative approaches to classify and prioritise compound responses.
Building robust analysis pipelines for large imaging datasets and interpreting and presenting results.
Coordinating research across academic collaborators and external partners.
Working with commercial suppliers and technology partners to integrate compound libraries, instrumentation and assay formats.
Contributing to publications, funding applications and scientific leadership.

title: Research Associate (Fixed Term (Internal candidates only)
description:
Internal applications are invited for  a full-time Postdoctoral Research Associate to join Dr Irving Aye's lab at the Department of Obstetrics & Gynaecology, University of Cambridge. Our main research interest is in understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying human placentation in normal pregnancies and in placenta-related pregnancy complications. To accomplish this, we are also interested in developing novel in vitro models to study cell-cell interactions. This exciting opportunity is funded by the Medical Research Council and work in the Aye lab is funded by additional grants from the MRC and the Evelyn Trust.
The post-holder must hold a PhD or MD/PhD in cell biology, biochemistry, reproductive biology or a closely related field and have proven track record of success in biomedical research. The post-holder will be responsible for running their own research projects and will collaborate with PhD students, research assistants and other post-docs both within the lab and across Cambridge. The post-holder will be supported to develop their own project within the lab's research theme.
Current work in the lab utilises state-of-the-art in vitro cultures (e.g., stem cells, primary cells, co-cultures, organoids), gene targeting approaches (Crispr/Cas9, sh/siRNA, overexpression), advanced molecular biology methods (e.g. bulk and single cell RNA-seq, methylation-seq, 6-letter-seq, ChIP-seq), fluorescence microscopy and metabolism assays (LC-MS, Seahorse Bioanalyzer). In vitro findings may be complemented by mouse models of placenta-specific gene manipulation to establish the physiological relevance, and the use of clinical samples to answer questions of clinical significance.

Developing and driving research objectives, including experimental design
Expertise in cell culture, immunohistochemistry, western blotting, RT-PCR, wet-lab sequencing protocols and other molecular biology techniques
Culturing human trophoblast stem cells, organoids and prima

title: Data Lifecycle Project Manager (Fixed Term)
location_text: Office of the School of Clinical Medicine
description:
The School of Clinical Medicine wishes to appoint a Data Lifecycle Project Manager to join their Research Governance team. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced and motivated individual to take a lead role in establishing routes for turning highly valuable research data assets into sustainable data products that could be better utilised both internally and by external researchers.
Clinical School researchers collect and generate an enormous amount of research data which is stored across various University IT platforms and cloud systems.  On completion of a specific research project there are few resources to maintain and access these data assets further for the benefit of other researchers both within and external to the University.  In essence few of these research datasets are FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable).
This fixed term full-time role will actively look at data sets held across the Clinical School, liaise with Cambridge University Hospitals (CUH) Research & Development team, the Clinical School Research Governance team and the Research Office to put together a policy and manual for researchers to enable these collated data sets to be sustainably managed throughout the data lifecycle and FAIR.
The role sits within the University Clinical Governance team but will require close liaison with the University Research Operations Office, the School of Clinical Medicine Computing Service (CSCS) and the University Information Services (UIS) within the University. The role holder will also need to liaise with other institutions on the Biomedical Campus including CUH R&D, Cambridge and Peterborough Foundation Trust R&D office and Cambridge University Health Partners.
Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available for 12 months in the first instance.
Once an offer of employment has been accepted, the successful candidate will be required to undergo a basic disclosure (criminal records check) check.

title: Postdoctoral Research Associate (Fixed Term)
description:
The Deane and Rayner laboratories at the Cambridge Institute for Medical Research are recruiting a Postdoctoral Research Associate to work as part of an ongoing team project that explores the function of a multi-gene family that is expanded in the genomes of Plasmodium vivax and other related neglected human malaria parasites.
The project builds on a recent publication that established that these tryptophan-rich antigens (TRAgs) have lipid binding activity (PMID: 37709739). This is a short-term position to produce high-quality purified TRAg proteins for structural and functional studies. It will be absolutely essential that the successful candidate has demonstrable experience in: protein expression using HEK293F-based mammalian expression systems; structure determination including X-ray crystallography of protein-ligand complexes; and biophysical characterisation of protein interactions such as using biolayer interferometry or isothermal titration calorimetry. The Board works closely with the Artistic Director and Executive Producer, bringing their experience and expertise as well as providing constructive challenge and support when needed.
Our Trustees are strong supporters of Fifth Word's work and our role in the theatre sector. They regularly attend performances and events to support the company and help build relationships with partners and supporters.
Our current trustees are Ellen O'Hara (current Chair), Jo McLeish, and Amanda Wallace.
All Trustees share responsibility for decisions made by the board. Each term lasts three years, with the option to renew for up to nine years total (or longer if the Board agrees).
Please note, this is a volunteer, unpaid role, but we cover reasonable out-of-pocket expenses. Trustees can live anywhere, as long as they are legally allowed to be a charity trustee in the UK.
New Trustees will receive an induction and support to help them understand Fifth Word and their responsibilities.

FOI Manager
The Domesday Book. Shakespeare’s will. Tweets from Downing Street. War time records. These are just some of the 11 million items held by The National Archives. With a collection like this – the largest in the world – it’s no surprise that we handle over five percent of all Freedom of Information (FOI) requests received by the Government. As FOI Manager, you’ll have a great opportunity to work with closed historical records. You’ll ensure decisions regarding their access are efficiently and appropriately managed to keep operations running smoothly. Join us and you’ll work in an organisation that offers great support and exceptional benefits.
About the role:
The majority of the FOI requests we receive are for closed historical information. Your key responsibilities will involve ensuring we comply with legal obligations set by FOI, EIR and DPA Acts. This includes managing FOI casework and FOI staff Assessors & Researchers - who undertake the bulk of review work. As well as managing the FOI caseload, you’ll be a source of expertise, guiding the Head of Centre and giving advice on difficult cases. As part of the FOI Management team, you’ll be responsible for deciding our legal position on appeals and tribunals. This means working closely with senior figures from The National Archives managers to information rights units across government. At the same time, you’ll promote FOI knowledge across the organisation. You’ll give updates on guidelines, consider feedback and shape future operations.

About us
Royal Museums Greenwich (RMG) is a collection of diverse historical sites. The sites are the National Maritime Museum, Cutty Sark, the Royal Observatory, and the Queen’s House. Each of these sites has a unique identity and a common purpose to serve our communities, through sharing our collections and expertise. We are a place to explore the sea, space, art and history, and our strategy ‘Charting Our Course’ puts people at the core of its success.
First Light
The Development Team secures vital funding to support core programming and public engagement, exhibitions, collections care and major capital projects at Royal Museums Greenwich. We work with philanthropists, companies and trusts & foundations, building a community of generous and loyal supporters from our Patrons Circle and legacies to major grants and corporate partners. Our current focus is to secure a team target of £2M revenue income in this financial year, and deliver the funding needed to deliver First Light, a landmark capital transformation of the Royal Observatory Greenwich.
First Light is an £85M project to deliver an ambitious schedule of much needed repair to the unique built heritage, vital capital improvements to the site plus an embedded programme of activities to build the nation’s science capital. A focus on physical, cultural, intellectual and financial access will ensure that everyone can enjoy, and benefit from, all the Observatory has to offer.
Aiming to break ground winter 2025 and reopen in spring 2028, First Light will affirm the Royal Observatory as THE centre for the public understanding and enjoyment of astronomy - a place of awe and wonder.

Head of Data and Information Policy
The National Archives (TNA) operates in an extremely varied, complex and sophisticated policy context. This role will be the chief adviser to the Keeper of Public Records and The National Archives’ Board on all aspects of data and information policy relating to how The National Archives operates and implements its strategy.
This role will lead, nurture and manage relationships with key strategic stakeholders on behalf of the Chief Executive and will support the Deputy Chief Executive in influencing the legislative and data policy landscape across government, so that the interests of The National Archives and the wider archive sector are protected, championed and, where possible, advanced.
This role will lead the work to realise The National Archives’ ministerially-endorsed strategic ambition to “develop proposals for legislative change to the Public Records Act 1958, and the wider regime for access to the historical public record”, in order to unlock the value of archival holdings in the digital age.
This role will be a senior member of the Government and Archives Leadership Directorate, supporting the Deputy Chief Executive to collectively drive delivery of the Directorate’s business. This role will also provide corporate leadership of The National Archives as a key member of its wider Senior Leadership Team, with collective accountability for organisational culture and successful delivery of The National Archives’ strategy.

You will work closely with multidisciplinary teams to identify opportunities, shape solutions and advocate for users throughout the product lifecycle.
